handoff.purpose: Define Shape dataclass fields and methods for serialization/signature/rendering, helper functions for name extraction and layout detection, and the beginning of the describe function for array-like objects.

symbols.name: Shape.names
symbols.note: tuple of strings for keys/columns, bounded

symbols.name: Shape.n_names
symbols.note: int, true count even when names are clipped

symbols.name: Shape.layout
symbols.note: str: C-contiguous, F-contiguous, strided, or empty

symbols.name: Shape.length
symbols.note: int, -1 when object has no length

symbols.name: Shape.to_dict
symbols.note: Serializes Shape to dict, includes element recursively

symbols.name: Shape.signature
symbols.note: Stable one-line form for comparison; includes family, type, dtype, dims, names/truncated, length

symbols.name: Shape.render
symbols.note: Debug-console line representation; includes type, dtype, dims/length, layout, nbytes, names

symbols.name: _names_of
symbols.note: Bounded, order-preserving name extraction; returns (shown_names, total_count, truncated_flag)

symbols.name: _layout_of
symbols.note: Returns layout string from obj.flags: C-contiguous, F-contiguous, strided, or empty

claims.text: "Bounded, order-preserving name extraction with the TRUE count kept."
claims.why: Function returns shown names (bounded by MAX_NAMES), total count, and truncated flag; order preserved by iterating over seq.

claims.text: "A stable one-line form, for comparing two observations or joining an observation against a declared type. Deterministic: names are already in a fixed order and nothing here consults a hash seed."
claims.why: Method constructs string from deterministic fields; no hash seed used.

claims.text: "The debug-console line this record stands in for."
claims.why: Method produces a string combining type, dtype, dims/length, layout, nbytes, names.

claims.text: "Describe one live object's SHAPE. Never reads a value."
claims.why: Function does not read values in this chunk; full implementation not shown.

claims.text: "``redact`` is called on every key/column name before it is stored and may return a replacement. Pass one whenever the observation could reach a model or leave the machine — a column name is data too."
claims.why: redact is applied in the array-like branch via generator expression; not all branches shown; claim about all keys/columns not fully verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: "A structured dtype IS a schema — surface its fields like columns."
claims.why: For array-like with dtype having names, fields are extracted via _names_of and stored as names/n_names.

observations.what: describe() uses _attr() which is not defined in this chunk; will raise NameError if not imported or defined elsewhere.
describe() uses _qualname() which is not defined in this chunk; will raise NameError if not imported or defined elsewhere.
describe() uses _human_bytes() in render method (line ~97) but not in this chunk; render calls _human_bytes but _human_bytes is not defined in this chunk.

In describe(), redact is called on generator expression 'red(f) for f in fields' but redact is a callable that should accept a string; the generator yields the result of red(f) for each f in fields; this is consistent with the docstring.
The array-like branch explicitly excludes objects with 'columns' attribute, likely to avoid pandas DataFrames which have both dtype/shape and columns.
